hero.headline: What we have built.
hero.lead: Seven projects in detail. The problem, what we built, and the numbers.

cases.client: AI quality control platform for a Dutch agritech company
cases.role: One senior engineer, end to end
cases.summary: Problem: industrial clients needed automated, 24/7 quality control on image data, in environments that each had their own security requirements. What we built: the full stack around computer-vision inference. NestJS API, Vue.js annotation interface, PostgreSQL, CI/CD and a hybrid deployment across Azure and on-premise. Production services and large image datasets were migrated to new hardware with zero data loss.
cases.approach: NVIDIA Triton for model serving (ResNet and YOLO), a modular NestJS API and a data pipeline with OCR and validation agents. Designed for high throughput with cost and reliability in mind.

stats.label: of images processed for quality control
enterprise client environments on one platform

cases.production: In production since Q3 2023 · zero-downtime deployments

diagram.footer: Hybrid on-prem + cloud · CI/CD · Docker · GPU inference 24/7
diagram.aria: Edge cameras send images through a cloud API to on-premise GPU inference with NVIDIA Triton and a NestJS API, feeding a Vue annotation UI and a PostgreSQL label store

cases.client: ArrowLancer: job platform for skilled migrants and sponsoring employers
cases.role: Own product, built by the studio
cases.summary: Problem: international professionals apply to jobs that will never sponsor a visa, and the job ad rarely says so. What we built: a platform that reads the career pages of Dutch companies itself, gives every job a sponsorship score, matches CVs and emails the matches. With a Moroccan edition, Stripe subscriptions and autonomous writers that publish daily SEO articles and social posts for five sites.
cases.approach: An LLM crawler with parallel workers and sponsorship scoring, a NestJS API on MongoDB, a Next.js frontend, all on Azure Container Apps. PostHog monitoring and an hourly watchdog keep the pipelines honest.
cases.production: Live on arrowlancer.com and arrowlancer.ma · since 2024

diagram.footer: Azure Container Apps · PostHog monitoring · hourly watchdog
diagram.aria: Company career pages are crawled by an LLM crawler with sponsorship scoring into a NestJS API with MongoDB and Stripe, serving a Next.js site, CV matching with email digests and daily SEO and social writers

cases.client: Mobile app, back office and website for a sportstech startup
cases.summary: Problem: an early-stage startup had to launch a mobile app, a back office and a public website at the same time, with a team that still had to be built. What we built: the React Native app with Unity game features, the React and Next.js back office and the website, on a NestJS backend with OAuth2 and Firebase Auth.
cases.approach: Architecture, sprint planning and code reviews for a team of 7 to 12 engineers. CI/CD on AWS and role-based access across mobile and web.
cases.production: Live on the App Store and Google Play · 2022 to 2023

diagram.footer: Three product streams on one backend · OAuth2 · AWS
diagram.aria: A React Native app with Unity scenes, a Next.js back-office and a public website share one NestJS API with OAuth2 and Firebase Auth, MongoDB and AWS CI/CD

cases.client: Screebl: SaaS dashboards for digital marketing agencies
cases.role: Full-stack engineer, from zero to live
cases.summary: Problem: agencies reported campaigns to clients through spreadsheets and loose PDFs. What we built: Screebl, a SaaS where a campaign spreadsheet becomes a live, branded client dashboard shared by secure link. With roles per agency and per client, an AI report assistant and six languages.
cases.approach: Nuxt 3 with Tailwind on the front, NestJS and MongoDB behind it, hierarchy-aware role-based access, OpenAI for report text and fill suggestions. Playwright end-to-end and visual regression tests, deployed on AWS.
cases.production: Live since 2025 · end-to-end tested on every release

diagram.footer: AWS · Playwright end-to-end and visual tests
diagram.aria: Campaign spreadsheets are uploaded to a NestJS API with hierarchy-aware roles and an OpenAI report assistant, rendered as Nuxt dashboards in six languages and shared by secure link

cases.summary: Problem: an app had to photograph receipts, read them, categorise them and analyse spending, with a separate OCR service that must be called securely. What we built: the full NestJS 11 backend with OCR integration, authentication, a categorisation engine and an analytics API, on Google Cloud with separate dev and production environments.
cases.approach: NestJS 11 with TypeORM on managed PostgreSQL, Cloud Run with CI/CD, service-to-service authentication to the OCR microservice, Firebase auth for users and object storage for the images.

diagram.footer: Google Cloud · separate dev and prod environments
diagram.aria: A mobile app with Firebase auth calls a NestJS API on Cloud Run, which uses a separate OCR microservice with service-to-service auth, stores data in managed PostgreSQL and object storage, and serves spending analytics

cases.client: PrjLab: a home for projects and their AI context
cases.role: Own product, built by the studio
cases.summary: Problem: code travels with git, but a project's AI context (instructions, memory, sessions) stays behind on one machine. What we built: a GitHub-like platform plus an open-source CLI that pushes, pulls and clones repositories together with their AI context. Private context is encrypted, sharing works and can be revoked.
cases.approach: Open-source CLI on npm, client-side encrypted storage, versioned context, public repositories and profiles. 150+ CLI tests, integration tests on PostgreSQL and browser tests for the platform.

stats.label: CLI tests on Linux, macOS, Windows

diagram.footer: Linux · macOS · Windows · integration and browser tests
diagram.aria: An open-source CLI encrypts a project's AI context on the client and pushes it with the git repository to the platform, which stores versions in PostgreSQL and supports revocable sharing and public repos

cases.client: Regulaitor: architecture audit for an AI compliance platform
cases.summary: Problem: a founding team with Regulaitor, an AI platform for screening customer calls wanted to know what had to happen before a reliable production release. What we did: reviewed the Node.js and React codebase on architecture, security and AI pipeline, and delivered a prioritised list of recommendations. This is the kind of work that is now our Production Readiness Audit package.
cases.approach: Code review per service and per data flow, transcription and LLM pipeline assessed on reliability and cost, a risk register with severity and owner, a plan for the first 30 days and for 90 days.
cases.production: Recommendations delivered to the founding team · 2025

diagram.footer: Written report · readout with the founding team
diagram.aria: A Node.js and React codebase for AI call screening is reviewed on architecture, security and AI pipeline, producing a risk register, prioritised fixes and a 90-day plan

terms.description: Terms of engagement for working with Jaize Tech, a sole proprietorship of A. Jaize based in IJlst, Netherlands.
terms.headline: Terms
terms.intro: Short, clear terms for working with me. No fine print, no legal theatre. If something isn't clear, just ask.

sections.p: Jaize Tech is a sole proprietorship of A. Jaize, software engineer. Based in IJlst, Friesland. KvK 42051769.

Software engineering, AI features, infrastructure work, and related technical services. We agree the scope of each engagement up front. What I'm not delivering goes in the proposal too, so there's no room for confusion.
Prices are fixed per engagement and agreed up front. No hidden costs. Invoicing happens per project or monthly for ongoing work. Payment terms are 14 days from invoice date unless we agree otherwise.
Something needs to change mid-engagement? No problem. We run a short change request with adjusted price and timeline. Both sides sign before the work shifts.
All code and deliverables I build for you belong to you once payment is complete. I may reference the work anonymously in my portfolio, unless we agree otherwise.
What you share with me stays between us. I'm happy to sign an NDA if you'd prefer. I expect the same from you for anything I show you during our conversations.

My liability is limited to the value of the specific engagement. I do my work as carefully as I can, but I don't guarantee outcomes from third parties like AI models, external APIs, or cloud providers.
If either of us wants to stop the engagement, put it in writing. Work already completed gets invoiced up to the cancellation date.
Dutch law applies to these terms. Disputes go to the competent court in Friesland.
Questions about these terms? Email me at abdellah@jaizetech.nl. I reply within 24 hours on business days.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: How Jaize Tech handles personal data from visitors and clients. A short, honest explanation. Analytics only with your consent.
privacy.headline: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Short explanation of what data I process and why. No pages of legal text. Just what you actually need to know.

sections.p: A. Jaize, sole proprietorship Jaize Tech, based in IJlst, Netherlands. KvK 42051769. For questions about your data: abdellah@jaizetech.nl.

What you fill in on the contact form: name, email address, optionally company name, and your message. For site statistics I use PostHog (servers in the EU). Without your consent it runs cookie-free: no cookies, no local storage, and your IP address is hashed, not stored. If you accept cookies in the banner, PostHog also records a replay of your visit (clicks, scrolling, page changes; everything you type is masked) and sets a cookie so it recognises your browser for a year. Changed your mind? Clear this site's cookies and site data in your browser and the banner asks again.
To read your message and reply. Nothing more, nothing less.
Until our conversation ends, then up to 2 more years for record-keeping. Want me to delete your data sooner? Send a mail and I'll do it within a week.

With Brevo for sending emails (they deliver my reply), with Cloudflare for hosting this site, and with PostHog (EU) for statistics and, only after your consent, session replays. That's it. No advertising networks, no data brokers, no selling of data.

You have the right to access, correct, and delete your data. You can also object to processing. Email abdellah@jaizetech.nl and I'll handle it within a week. Not satisfied? You can complain to the Dutch Data Protection Authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens).

Messages you send via the contact form go through an encrypted connection. I store your data in my email (Gmail with 2FA) and nowhere else. If there were ever a data breach, I'd report it within 72 hours per GDPR rules.
If I update this policy, the date at the top changes. Significant changes get announced on my site.
